Used Lamborghini Revuelto Hits the Used Car Market Stateside, What’s Your Take on the Price?
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec
Supercars come in numerous sizes and shapes these days, as the offer has never been so vast. Still, the majority of the petrolhead crowd has a favorite brand, and if yours is Lamborghini, then you have come to the right place, because we just encountered this Revuelto that is searching for a new home in the New World as we speak.
The model needs no introduction, especially if you have a soft spot for the Raging Bull’s modern-day machines. That’s because it is the company’s new-age flagship supercar, which replaced the Aventador some three years ago. The latter was preceded by the Murcielago, Diablo, Countach, and Miura in this order, and do you know what each and every one of these models has in common, besides the Lamborghini logo?
Well, they all feature a V12. And the automaker wasn’t willing to drop it for the modern-day Revuelto . That’s great news for the gearhead crowd, as not only does this model feature a great V12 mounted behind the passenger compartment, but it is a naturally aspirated unit, too, for faster responses. Nevertheless, it does feature electric assistance in order to meet the latest emission regulations, and it is a plug-in hybrid model in case you forgot.
The peak output is officially rated at 1,001 hp (747 kW/1,015 ps), and that’s more than the original Bugatti Veyron. The Revuelto takes only 2.5 seconds to sprint to 62 mph (100 kph), and pushes up to 217 mph (350 kph). The Revuelto SV, which is a significantly upgraded variant, has 1,050 hp (783 kW/1,065 ps) in total, is one-tenth of a second faster, and will reach 216 mph (348 kph). And that’s not a typo, because these numbers can be easily verified online.
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec Buying a brand new Lamborghini Revuelto means paying over $600,000 for the 2027 model year, and that’s definitely no bargain. The Revuelto SV is even more expensive, as it will set you back nearly $750,000. And that’s before the often-greedy dealer markups, as well as before checking any boxes on the options list. But how much is a used example?
Just because you are willing to buy used does not mean that you will pay pennies on the dollar. In fact, the market today shows that the Revuelto still tends to fetch over $600,000, and some copies can easily exceed $700,000, whereas others have just dropped below the $600K mark. A good machine requires blowing more than $600K, for what it’s worth. And this brings us to the supercar pictured in the gallery, which is for sale today in USA.
It is advertised by @limitedspec on social media, which reveals that the odometer reads 6,187 miles (9,957 km), and it is not considered a low-mileage example, because it is on the exotic side of things. Therefore, we can say that this car has seen plenty of action ever since it rolled off the line a few years ago. A low-mileage one has less than 1,000 miles (1,600 km) under its belt.
This Lamborghini Revuelto has a Bianco Monocerus paint finish beneath the wrap, which is matte black. The glossy black wheels, which spin around the red brake calipers, appear to be original, and on the inside, it offers a mix of white and black leather and Alcantara upholstery, with white piping and stitching, and the Lamborghini logo embroidered into the headrests.
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec It looks like the windows have been tinted, so the wrap is not the only mod, but for what it’s worth, this supercar definitely looks great. In fact, it is almost perfect, this writer would say, as the model rocks the stealth fighter jet-like look like a champ. The only thing needed to look perfect, in my opinion, would be a black Alcantara interior with a few red touches here and there for a bit of contrast.
But most people have a favorite look when it comes to the Lamborghini Revuelto, and if your happens to coincide with the one pictured in the gallery above, and you have enough zeros in the bank to put your money where your mouth is, then you should reach out to the vendor with an offer. After all, what’s the worse that they can say? No?
We still haven’t told you how much this Italian supercar costs, and if you want to write your name on the dotted line, you will have to fork out $639,980. That was the asking price at the time of writing. Interested parties should know that this Lamborghini Revuelto is located in Miami, Florida, and that’s everything we know about it, because the vendor hasn’t had much to say about this exotic ride in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page.
So, if you were shopping for a nice Lamborghini Revuelto and you came across this one, would you have blown $640K on it? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Limited Spec Automotive (@limitedspec)
